functions.name: run_tmux (port of tmux())
functions.behavior: Spawn `tmux` with the given argv (no shell), capture stdout as UTF-8 text, and return only stdout. This is the single choke point for every tmux invocation; every other function here and in other modules calls it. The Python version returns result.stdout verbatim (a String), NOT trimmed.
functions.side_effects: Forks the tmux binary as a child process (subprocess.run). Reads no stdin. Inherits the ambient environment (notably $TMUX so tmux talks to the right server).
edge_cases: PARITY-CRITICAL: the return code is completely ignored and stderr is completely discarded. A failed tmux call (server gone, bad target) must yield an EMPTY string, never an error/panic. Rust port must NOT propagate an Err or unwrap; on spawn failure or non-zero exit it must return "" (or the captured stdout, which is typically empty).

stdout is decoded as text=True (UTF-8 with the locale). Non-UTF-8 bytes: Python text mode would raise; in practice tmux output is UTF-8. Port should decode lossily to avoid a panic that Python would not have (Python would rarely hit this on real tmux output, but lossy is the safe parity choice).
No trimming is done by run_tmux itself; individual callers do their own .strip()/.splitlines(). Preserve that: return the raw stdout including any trailing newline.

args is a variadic in Python (tmux(*args)); some callers pass a bare ";" element as a tmux command separator (see focus). The argv vector must pass ";" through as its own element, unquoted, unescaped.

functions.name: strip_status_prefix
functions.behavior: Drop the leading status glyph Claude Code prefixes onto a pane title (a spinner braille frame while working, `✳` when idle). Partition the trimmed title on the FIRST ASCII space; if a space was found AND the head token contains no alphanumeric character, return the trimmed remainder; otherwise return the whole trimmed title. Used inside fetch_windows to produce pane_titles for daemon-session title matching (assoc module).
functions.side_effects: None (pure). Included in the tmux module only because fetch_windows is its sole caller; may instead live in `rows`/`labels`.
edge_cases: PARITY: Python `str.partition(' ')` splits on the first literal space (U+0020) only, not on tabs or other Unicode whitespace. Do not use a generic whitespace split.

PARITY: the alnum test is Python `str.isalnum()`, which is Unicode-aware — non-ASCII letters/digits count as alphanumeric. A braille spinner char and `✳` are NOT alphanumeric, so they are stripped; a real title starting with a word is kept. Rust must use a Unicode-aware is_alphanumeric over ALL chars of the head (`any(c.isalnum())`), not just ASCII.
Title with no space at all: partition sep is empty -> return title.strip() unchanged.
Title starting with a space (empty head): head has no alnum -> returns rest.strip(). e.g. "  foo" -> "foo".
Leading/trailing whitespace on the input is stripped in both branches (Python .strip() = strip ASCII+Unicode whitespace; use trim()).

functions.name: fetch_windows
functions.signature: fn fetch_windows(sidebar_pane: &str) -> FetchResult  // FetchResult bundles: windows: Vec<Window>, pane_to_window: HashMap<PaneId, WindowRef>, sidebars: HashSet<PaneId>, pane_paths: HashMap<PaneId,String>, pane_progress: HashMap<PaneId,(String,Option<u32>)>, pane_titles: HashMap<PaneId,String>, pane_pids: HashMap<PaneId,u32>, sidebar_active: bool
functions.behavior: Two tmux calls build the whole window/pane model. (1) `tmux list-windows -F '#{window_id}\t#{window_index}\t#{window_name}\t#{window_active}'` -> one Window{id,index,name,active,panes=[]} per line. (2) `tmux list-panes -s -F '#{window_id}\t#{pane_id}\t#{pane_index}\t#{pane_active}\t#{@wrangler_sidebar}\t#{pane_pb_state}\t#{pane_pb_progress}\t#{pane_pid}\t#{pane_current_path}\t#{pane_title}'` -> for each pane, populate the lookup maps and, for real (non-sidebar) panes, append a Pane{id,index,active,title,pb_state,pb_progress} to its window's panes list. Returns the 8-tuple. Window/index/name are kept as STRINGS (index is not parsed to int here).
functions.side_effects: Two tmux subprocess calls. No writes. Pure read of tmux state.
edge_cases: PARITY: list-windows line parse is `line.split('\t', 3)` = split into at most 4 fields (maxsplit 3). window_name is field 3; a tab inside window_name would corrupt the parse (name rarely contains tabs). Replicate maxsplit=3 semantics (splitn(4,'\t')), NOT a naive split that would panic on an unexpected field count.

PARITY: list-panes line parse is `line.split('\t', 9)` = at most 10 fields (maxsplit 9). pane_title is the trailing free-form field and may contain anything except a tab; pane_current_path is assumed tab-free. Use splitn(10,'\t'). A line with fewer than 10 tab fields would make Python raise ValueError (unpack); the port should skip/guard such malformed lines rather than panic — but note Python does NOT guard, so in practice tmux always emits 10 fields.
active flag comparison is exact string `== '1'` for window_active and pane_active.

@wrangler_sidebar detection: a pane is a sidebar if `flag == '1'` OR `pid == SIDEBAR_PANE`. The OR on SIDEBAR_PANE is load-bearing: a just-spawned sidebar may not yet have its @wrangler_sidebar option set (spawn race), yet it must still classify itself as a sidebar and be skipped from the pane tree.

sidebar_active is set ONLY on the branch `pid == SIDEBAR_PANE` (to `active == '1'`); it defaults to false and stays false if this sidebar's own pane never appears in the pane list. Do not set it for other sidebar panes.
A pane whose window_id is not in the by_id map (window not returned by list-windows) is silently skipped (`if wid not in by_id: continue`).
pane_pid: `int(pane_pid) if pane_pid.isdigit() else 0`. isdigit() is true only for all-ASCII-digit non-empty strings (no sign, no whitespace). Empty -> 0. Store 0 for missing.

pb_progress: `int(pb_progress) if pb_progress.isdigit() else None`. Empty (old tmux, or no OSC report) -> None. pane_progress[pid] = (pb_state, progress) where pb_state is the raw string (may be '', 'hidden', 'paused', 'indeterminate', 'normal', etc.). On a tmux that does not know pb_state/pb_progress these format vars expand to empty -> ('', None) = 'no progress'. Preserve the empty-string state exactly (downstream progress_indicator/rows distinguishes it).

ITERATION ORDER is load-bearing: windows are kept in list-windows output order; panes are appended to each window in list-panes -s output order. build_rows renders the pane tree in this order (└─ on the last, ├─ otherwise), so the Vec<Pane> order must match tmux's emission order exactly. Use ordered Vecs, not sets, for windows/panes.
sidebars is a set of pane ids (order irrelevant); the sidebar occupancy / spawn-race check in main iterates it.
Real pane's title stored two ways: the tree row keeps the RAW `title` (with glyph), while pane_titles[pid] stores strip_status_prefix(title) for daemon-session title matching. Keep both.

pane_paths, pane_pids, pane_progress are populated for ALL panes including sidebars (they are keyed before the sidebar `continue`); pane_titles and the window.panes append happen ONLY for real panes (after the continue). Preserve this split.

functions.name: window_real_panes
functions.behavior: `tmux list-panes -t <win_id> -F '#{pane_id}\t#{@wrangler_sidebar}'`; return the pane ids (in output order) that are NOT sidebars — i.e. flag != '1' AND pid != SIDEBAR_PANE. Used by focus() to land on a real pane, and could be used by glue.
functions.side_effects: One tmux subprocess call (scoped to one window, no -s).
edge_cases: Line parse uses `partition('\t')` -> (pid, sep, flag); a line with no tab yields flag='' (falsy != '1' -> treated as real, if pid also != SIDEBAR_PANE). Replicate partition semantics (split_once).
SIDEBAR_PANE is excluded even though its @wrangler_sidebar may or may not be '1' — the explicit pid check mirrors fetch_windows so the calling sidebar never picks itself as a focus target.
Order preserved (Vec, first element used by focus).

functions.name: focus
functions.behavior: Select a window and (best-effort) a real pane within it. If pane_id is given (Some/non-empty), use it directly. Otherwise query the window's active pane via `tmux display-message -p -t <win_id> '#{pane_id}\t#{@wrangler_sidebar}'`; if that active pane is a sidebar (flag == '1' OR == SIDEBAR_PANE), replace the target with window_real_panes(win_id)[0] (or None if the window has no real panes). Then run a single chained tmux invocation: `select-window -t <win_id>` and, only if a target pane was resolved, `; select-pane -t <target>`.
functions.side_effects: One tmux read (display-message) only in the no-pane-arg path; one tmux mutating call (select-window [; select-pane]) that moves the user's focus. Possibly a second read via window_real_panes.
edge_cases: PARITY: the final command is built as a single argv list `['select-window','-t',win,';','select-pane','-t',pane]` passed to one `tmux(...)` call — the literal `;` is a tmux command separator element, so both commands run in one tmux process. Do NOT run two separate tmux processes; and do NOT let a shell interpret the `;`. In Rust, pass ";" as its own Command arg (tmux parses it, the shell is never involved since there is no shell).

pane_id given as empty string is falsy in Python (`if not target_pane`) -> treated as absent and the active-pane lookup runs. Model this: Option::None OR Some("") both trigger the lookup. Recommend normalizing empty -> None.

If the active pane is a real pane, target_pane stays None and ONLY select-window runs (no select-pane) — focus lands wherever tmux puts it in that window. This is intentional: don't force a pane when the active one is already real.
If active pane is a sidebar and the window has NO real panes, target_pane is None -> only select-window runs.
display-message output is .strip()'d then partition('\t'); active pane id is head, flag is tail.

functions.name: activate
functions.signature: fn activate(item: &Row) -> ()  // calls focus(item.win.id, item.pane.as_deref(), sidebar_pane)
functions.behavior: Thin adapter: focus(item['win']['id'], item.get('pane')). A window row has no 'pane' key (-> None -> real-pane resolution); a pane row and an agent row carry a 'pane' (-> focus that exact pane). Bound to Enter/click activation in the client/main loop.
edge_cases: item.get('pane') returns None for window rows (key absent) — Rust Row model must make `pane` Optional so window/pane/agent rows dispatch identically to Python's dict.get.

functions.name: sidebar occupancy / spawn-race check (inline in main, tmux-owned invariant)
functions.signature: fn should_self_exit(sidebars: &HashSet<PaneId>, pane_to_window: &Map, me: &WindowRef, sidebar_pane: &str) -> bool
functions.behavior: Not a standalone Python function but a tmux-model invariant to port: after fetch_windows, the sidebar exits (a) if pane_to_window has no entry for SIDEBAR_PANE (its own pane vanished), (b) if any OTHER sidebar pane p occupies the same window `me` AND has a lower numeric id than SIDEBAR_PANE (spawn race — the lower-id sidebar wins), or (c) if `me['panes']` is empty (no real panes left; tmux then closes the window).
functions.side_effects: Decides process exit (return from main). No tmux calls itself.
edge_cases: PARITY: numeric pane-id comparison is `int(p[1:]) < int(SIDEBAR_PANE[1:])` — pane ids are tmux `%N` strings; p[1:] strips the leading `%` and parses the rest as an integer. Port must strip the '%' sigil and compare as integers, NOT lexicographically ('%10' < '%9' lexically but 10 > 9 numerically).
The comparison uses identity `pane_to_window.get(p) is me` (same Window object). In Rust use window-id equality against me's id.
Only lower-id sidebars trigger exit, so exactly one sidebar per window survives a race (the lowest %N).

functions.name: spawn (port of spawn.sh)
functions.signature: fn spawn(if_active: bool, win: Option<&str>) -> Result<()>  // glue subcommand
functions.behavior: Ensure a target window has exactly-or-at-least-not-yet a sidebar, then split one in. Steps: (1) win defaults to `tmux display-message -p '#{window_id}'`. (2) if if_active, run `tmux list-panes -s -F '#{@wrangler_sidebar}'` and exit 0 unless some line contains '1' (session has sidebars = toggled on). (3) if `tmux list-panes -t <win> -F '#{@wrangler_sidebar}'` contains '1', exit 0 (window already has one). (4) width = `tmux show-option -gqv @wrangler-width`, default 32. (5) `tmux split-window -d -f -h -b -l <width> -t <win> -P -F '#{pane_id}' "python3 '<script_dir>/sidebar.py'"` capturing the new pane id. (6) `tmux set-option -p -t <pane> @wrangler_sidebar 1`.
functions.side_effects: Creates a tmux pane running the sidebar; tags it with the @wrangler_sidebar pane option. In the Rust port the spawned command becomes the wrangler binary's sidebar subcommand rather than `python3 sidebar.py`.
edge_cases: PARITY: the presence tests use `grep -q 1` (substring match for '1'). @wrangler_sidebar values are only ever '1' or empty, so substring is safe; replicate as 'any line == "1"' (cleaner and behaviorally identical here).

DEFAULT WIDTH 32 here is a DIFFERENT constant from min_width's default 24 (@wrangler-min-width). @wrangler-width = initial spawn width (default 32); @wrangler-min-width = enforced floor (default 24). Do not conflate.

split flags: -d (don't switch to it), -f (full-height, span the whole window), -h (horizontal split = side-by-side), -b (place BEFORE = left of target), -l <width> (size in columns), -P -F '#{pane_id}' (print the new pane id).
set -euo pipefail semantics: any failing tmux call aborts. The two early-exit `grep` checks are the only ones allowed to 'fail' (via the if-guards).
Script dir resolution (BASH_SOURCE dirname) — in Rust use the wrangler executable path / a known install path instead.

functions.name: toggle (port of toggle.sh)
functions.behavior: The on/off switch. (1) sidebars = `tmux list-panes -s -F '#{pane_id} #{@wrangler_sidebar}'` filtered to lines whose 2nd field EQUALS 1 (awk `$2 == 1`), taking field 1 (pane id). (2) If any: for each, `tmux kill-pane -t <pane>` ignoring errors, then exit. (3) Else (turning on): `rm -f <STATE_DIR>/width`, then for each window id from `tmux list-windows -F '#{window_id}'`, call spawn(win) (no --if-active).
functions.side_effects: Either kills every sidebar pane in the session, or deletes the shared width file and spawns one sidebar per window. Deleting width resets width sync so all fresh sidebars negotiate from the @wrangler-width default.
edge_cases: PARITY: the filter is awk EXACT `$2 == 1` (numeric/string equality on the second whitespace-field), NOT the substring `grep -q 1` used in spawn.sh. A pane whose flag is empty prints '%id ' (field 2 empty) and is excluded. Port must compare the flag field for exact '1'.
kill-pane errors are swallowed (`2>/dev/null || true`) — a pane that dies between listing and killing must not abort the loop.
The width file is removed with -f (no error if absent). Path is `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/tmux-agent-wrangler/width` — same STATE_DIR/WIDTH_FILE the sidebar uses.
Turn-off is detected by 'any sidebar exists', turn-on spawns unconditionally per window (spawn.sh's per-window guard prevents doubles).
The single space separator between pane_id and flag in the -F string: parse on whitespace, not tab.

functions.name: focus_key (port of focus.sh)
functions.signature: fn focus_key() -> Result<()>  // glue subcommand (bound to @wrangler-focus-key)
functions.behavior: Give keyboard focus to the CURRENT window's sidebar pane, if it has one. (1) pane = first line of `tmux list-panes -F '#{pane_id} #{@wrangler_sidebar}'` (NOTE: no -s, so current window only) whose 2nd field == 1, taking field 1 (awk `$2 == 1 {print $1; exit}`). (2) If found: `tmux select-pane -t <pane>` then `tmux send-keys -t <pane> C-l`. (3) If none: no-op (never spawns).
functions.side_effects: Moves focus to the sidebar pane and sends a literal Ctrl-L keystroke to it. The sidebar's input loop treats C-l as a redraw request, so the focus highlight repaints immediately rather than waiting up to one poll interval (matches the mouse-click path).
edge_cases: PARITY: list-panes here has NO -s flag (current window scope), unlike spawn/toggle which use -s (session scope). Do not add -s.
awk takes the FIRST matching pane and exits; if a window somehow had two sidebars, only the first (list order) is focused.
Exact `$2 == 1` match again (not substring).
send-keys C-l is a SEPARATE tmux invocation after select-pane; both must run. C-l is tmux's key notation for Ctrl-L (not a literal string 'C-l').
A window with no sidebar pane produces empty output -> the whole body is skipped (no-op); must not error or spawn.

parity_risks: run_tmux MUST swallow all errors: non-zero exit and stderr are discarded, return stdout-or-empty. Any Rust idiom that propagates an error (unwrap/?, Command::status().success()) diverges — a dead tmux server yields "", and callers (splitlines over empty = no rows) degrade gracefully. Downstream, main returns/exits when fetch_windows yields no windows or no self-pane, so an over-eager error would change control flow.

Tab-delimited field parsing uses Python maxsplit: list-windows split('\t',3)=splitn(4), list-panes split('\t',9)=splitn(10). The trailing field (window_name / pane_title) legitimately holds spaces/glyphs; only a tab inside it breaks parsing (rare). Use splitn with the exact limit; do not use a plain split that yields a variable field count.

Sidebar classification double-rule `flag=='1' OR pid==SIDEBAR_PANE` (in fetch_windows AND window_real_panes) covers the spawn race where a new sidebar's pane option isn't set yet. Dropping the pid check would make a fresh sidebar list itself as a real pane and recurse into its own tree.

sidebar_active is a STICKY-default false, set only when this sidebar's own pane is seen with pid==SIDEBAR_PANE; it gates has_focus in main. Setting it for any sidebar pane, or defaulting true, changes which sidebar draws the selection bar.
Pane-id numeric comparison strips the '%' sigil (p[1:]) and compares as integers; lexical comparison of '%N' strings is wrong (spawn-race tiebreak picks the lowest %N).

strip_status_prefix relies on Unicode-aware isalnum over the head token and partitions on the first ASCII space only. ASCII-only is_alphanumeric or generic-whitespace splitting would mis-strip non-ASCII titles or the braille/✳ glyphs. Empty title and no-space title are distinct paths — an EMPTY title never yields a match downstream in assoc (guard preserved there, but strip returns '' cleanly here).

Iteration ORDER of windows (list-windows order) and panes (list-panes -s order, appended) is load-bearing for the rendered tree and last-pane branch glyph; use ordered Vecs, never HashSets/HashMaps, for the window/pane sequences. Only `sidebars` may be a set.
process_under-style bounded loops appear elsewhere; here the only bound is the spawn-race check which is not looping but the model must not assume unique pane ids across a server restart.

spawn.sh grep -q 1 (substring) vs toggle.sh/focus.sh awk $2==1 (exact) are DIFFERENT match semantics in the originals; safe because values are only '1'/empty, but the Rust port should encode exact-equality everywhere and not reintroduce a substring bug that would match a pane id or width containing '1'.
Two distinct width defaults: @wrangler-width=32 (initial spawn column count) and @wrangler-min-width=24 (enforced floor). Conflating them changes spawn geometry or the sync floor.

focus's chained `select-window -t win ; select-pane -t pane` is ONE tmux process using ';' as tmux's own command separator (no shell). Splitting into two processes or shell-quoting the ';' changes atomicity/semantics; omitting select-pane when target is None is intentional (leave tmux's active pane).
toggle deletes STATE_DIR/width on turn-ON (not off); focus.sh's C-l nudge and the no-op-when-absent guards are behavioral contracts other modules (client, width) rely on.

In the Rust port the spawned sidebar command replaces `python3 '<dir>/sidebar.py'` with the wrangler binary's sidebar subcommand; the @wrangler_sidebar pane option and TMUX_PANE-derived SIDEBAR_PANE identity must be preserved exactly since every 'is this a sidebar' decision keys off the option (never the pane command).
